category_title: Year 4 pupil with ADHD symptoms (hyperactivity, impulsivity, and learning difficulties)
minimal_context: Yiannis is assigned an independent writing task during the 90-minute Literacy hour.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are starting our Literacy hour now. Please take out your notebook and work on your own to write a text about your weekend.

STUDENT: (Stumps his feet under the desk) I don't want to work on my own. Writing is too hard.

TUTOR: Just try your best to start forming your sentences.

STUDENT: (Nervously moves his palms back and forth on his thighs) I went to the park and then I saw a dog and then we played and then we went home and then I ate dinner and then...

TUTOR: Keep going, you need to write more than that.

STUDENT: (Flaps his arms) No! I refuse to do this on my own anymore! I can't form the sentences!

options.A: Maintain a ratio of praise statements to error correction statements ranging from 3:1 or 5:1 to 10:1 during the Literacy hour.
options.B: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during instruction in the 90-minute Literacy hour.
options.C: Make lists of activities for the day at the beginning of each session, and tape the class timetable to his desk.
options.D: Proactively contact parents (using a translator if needed) to share both successes and concerns regarding his independent writing.
